newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 22.

text.p: Marubeni Corp and leading U.S. electricity wholesaler Sithe Energies Inc SYT.N plan to invest $2 billion through the year to 2000 to build about 50 power plants mainly in Asia in order to meet the region's growing demand for power. They will build the first plant in China by the end of 1998, followed by other Southeast Asian countries, including Indonesia and Thailand. Other plants will be built in North and South America.

Mitsubishi Corp may delist from stock exchanges in Sapporo, Niigata, Kyoto, Hiroshima and Fukuoka because it feels the exchanges offer few benefits in trading its stock, with comparatively low volume. But it will stay listed on the Tokyo and Osaka Stock Exchanges.

Sumitomo Rubber Industries Ltd is expected to have an operating profit of less than nine billion yen for the year ended December, about one billion yen below an initial projection. This is due to a drop in retail prices of tyres and a rise in raw materials prices.

Japan Synthetic Rubber Co Ltd and Nippon Zeon Co Ltd are expected to report increased pre-tax profits for the year to March, thanks to imroved profits from exports and growing new businesses. Japan Synthetic will see its profits rise by 41 percent to 11.5 billion yen and Nippon Zeon by 31 percent to six billion yen.

Hino Motors Ltd will cut regular working hours by five minutes per day effective from April 1 after the Confederation of Japan Automobile Workers' Unions demanded last spring that employers should cut daily work by 20 minutes.
Hitachi Ltd plans to invest a total of 40 billion yen on manufacturing facilities for wireless communications equipment over the next three years, mainly exchangers for cellular phone communications.
Nissan Diesel Motor Co Ltd and Samsung Heavy Industries Co Ltd have agreed to start using auto parts procured by Samsung from South Korean manufacturers in large trucks from May.

Under the agreement, Samsung will make large purchases of 33 types of auto parts for large trucks, including press-moulded brackets, aluminium steps and battery covers made of resin, and sell them to Nissan Diesel as well as using them itself.

Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd, Kanematsu Corp and Nippon Yakin Kogyo Co Ltd will purchase a 30 percent stake in an Indonesian stainless steel company to make 50,000 tonnes of stainless steel annually from October. Asian demand for stainless steel is growing. Total investment in the project will be $60 million.
